advisor.summary: Two very different products travel under the wellness label, and this record exists chiefly to hold the line between them. Legitimate: employer benefits that are actual medical care — screenings, immunizations, smoking-cessation and disease-management programs — excludable under §105(b) and §106 through a compliant plan, plus trivial perks under §132(e); modest, unglamorous, real. Illegitimate: the heavily marketed fixed-indemnity wellness schemes that cycle pay through pre-tax premiums and return it as supposedly untaxed cash. CCA 202323006 answers those directly: cash paid without regard to unreimbursed medical expenses is wages, subject to income and employment tax. The advisory posture is caution-first — implement the legitimate design, decline the scheme in writing, and insulate the client's broader plan from the taint.
mechanics: Genuine wellness benefits that constitute medical care under §213(d) — biometric screenings, flu shots, cessation and disease-management programs — are excludable under §105(b) and §106 when delivered through a plan that clears the same ACA market-reform analysis as any other reimbursement arrangement.
General-health perks are not medical care: gym memberships, fitness trackers, and wellness stipends are ordinarily taxable wages, and only trivial items fit within the §132(e) de minimis exclusion.

The marketed scheme's anatomy is consistent: pre-tax salary reductions purchase a fixed-indemnity wellness policy whose cash benefits — paid for watching videos or completing checklists — roughly return the premium, and promoters claim the round trip erases FICA.

CCA 202323006 holds that fixed-indemnity payments made without regard to actual unreimbursed §213(d) expenses fall outside the §105(b) exclusion: they are wages subject to withholding and FICA, and the promised savings are merely unpaid employment tax.

An honest design routes real medical care through the group plan or a compliant HRA, reports taxable perks on the W-2, and documents the decision to decline indemnity pitches — the client file should show each pitch was evaluated and refused.

authority.note: The legitimate exclusion: employer-provided medical care, including preventive and wellness services qualifying as medical care under a compliant plan.
Defines medical care — the test gym memberships and general-wellness stipends fail.
Holds that fixed-indemnity wellness payments made without regard to unreimbursed medical expenses are wages subject to income and employment taxes — the direct answer to the marketed schemes.
The de minimis fringe — the only narrow home for trivial wellness perks.
The market-reform framework every wellness reimbursement arrangement must clear if it constitutes a group health plan.

requirements: Excludable benefits confined to actual §213(d) medical care delivered under a written, ACA-compliant plan.
Taxable perks — gym stipends, fitness gear — reported in W-2 wages.
No arrangement whose economics depend on pre-tax premiums cycling back to employees as untaxed cash.
Documentation tying each reimbursement to a specific medical service or unreimbursed expense.
risks: The wellness-indemnity schemes are the headline risk, and CCA 202323006 is the controlling ruling: participating employers owe back FICA and withholding, deposit and accuracy penalties, and W-2 corrections — and promoter reliance offers thin protection when the promoter's own materials advertise the tax result.
Even legitimate reimbursement features are group health plans; a standalone, non-compliant design faces the §4980D excise at $100 per employee per day.
Misclassified perks — gym stipends left off the W-2 — seed small, pervasive payroll errors that compound across years.

Preparer exposure is real: signing returns that reflect a known indemnity scheme implicates preparer penalties and Office of Professional Responsibility standards — which is why the firm's declination belongs in writing.
stateNotes: Conformity: states following federal wage definitions tax the scheme payments exactly as the CCA describes, and state employment-tax bases stack atop the federal problem.
PTET: no PTET interaction — this record concerns payroll characterization, not entity income; any legitimate benefit deduction simply reduces the pass-through base before a PTET computation.

Missouri: conforms through RSMo §143.121, and Missouri withholding and unemployment contributions follow the federal wage recharacterization — a failed scheme creates state payroll exposure on top of the federal.
reviewChecklist: Every wellness dollar inventoried: medical care, taxable perk, or scheme.
Any indemnity-style program identified, quantified, and calendared for unwind.
Written declination memo on file for any active pitch.
Taxable perks confirmed on the W-2 going forward; prior years assessed for materiality.
Legitimate benefits mapped onto a compliant plan design.

client.teaser: That wellness pitch in your inbox has a tax problem — here is the version that holds up.
client.headline: Wellness benefits: the real thing, not the sales pitch
plainEnglish: You may have seen a program that sounds too good to be true. Employees join a wellness plan, do a few easy tasks, and everyone saves big on payroll taxes at no real cost. The IRS has publicly rejected that exact idea. The savings are just unpaid payroll tax, and employers who sign up owe it later, with penalties.
We would rather you hear this from us than from an auditor. A program that promises free money through payroll paperwork is not planning. It is a bill that has not arrived yet.

The honest version is worth doing at the right size. Your business can offer real health benefits — screenings, flu shots, counseling, help to quit smoking — tax-free through a proper plan. Gym perks are fine too; they are simply taxable pay, and we report them cleanly so they never become a problem.
client.analogy: A machine that turns payroll taxes into free cash is not really a machine — it is a loan from a future audit. Real wellness benefits are like a good pair of boots: modest, useful, built to last.
benefits: Real health benefits, delivered tax-free the right way
A documented reason to say no to the programs being pitched to you
Clean payroll treatment of perks — no surprises later
steps: WE review every wellness dollar you spend and every pitch you have received.
WE set up the tax-free benefits correctly and put taxable perks on the W-2.
YOU send us the next wellness pitch before you sign anything.
WE unwind any problem program before it gets bigger.
clientCommitments: Run wellness vendor pitches by us before you enroll
Put gym and fitness perks through payroll, not around it
